nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Rare disease WES analysis: germline variant calling, annotation, and candidate variant prioritization from the patient's whole-exome sequencing data | germline short-variant calling and annotation from paired-end whole-exome FASTQ (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller/DeepVariant, VEP annotation) with rare-disease variant filtering and prioritization → ranked annotated VCF of candidate causal variants

Rare disease RNA-seq analysis: process the patient's RNA-seq to detect expression outliers and aberrant splicing events that support variant interpretation | bulk RNA-seq processing for rare disease diagnostics (alignment and quantification, then expression outlier detection OUTRIDER-style and aberrant splicing detection FRASER-style) → per-gene expression outliers and splicing outliers with p-values

Integrate the WES candidate variants with the RNA-seq expression/splicing outliers to produce a final ranked list of candidate causal genes for the rare disease workup | integration of germline exome variant candidates with transcriptome expression and splicing outlier results — multi-omics concordance analysis → single ranked candidate causal gene/variant list with combined evidence scores

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

WES germline variant calling and annotation for rare disease | germline variant calling and clinical annotation from whole-exome sequencing FASTQ or BAM files (SNVs, indels, and CNVs) → annotated candidate variant table (VCF/TSV)

RNA-seq aberrant expression and aberrant splicing detection for rare disease | detection of aberrant gene expression and aberrant splicing from paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ or BAM files (OUTRIDER/FRASER) → outlier gene expression and aberrant splicing event table

Integrate WES genomic variants with RNA-seq aberrant expression and splicing evidence | multimodal integration of genomic variants (WES) with transcriptomic outliers (RNA-seq aberrant expression and splicing) → prioritized causal gene and variant report

Whole-exome sequencing rare disease analysis: germline short-variant calling, VEP annotation, and HPO-based variant prioritization from WES FASTQ data | germline short-variant calling, annotation, and rare disease prioritization from WES paired-end FASTQ (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller, VEP annotation, HPO/phenotype-based prioritization) → annotated VCF with prioritized candidate pathogenic variants

Guide RNA assignment from Perturb-seq CRISPR screen data — decode guide barcodes from single-cell transcriptome reads or direct capture, assign each cell to a perturbation group, producing a cell × guide assignment matrix. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575 (DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013). | guide RNA assignment from Perturb-seq single-cell CRISPR screen data — decode guide barcode from transcriptome reads or direct capture amplicon, assign cells to perturbation groups, generate cell × guide assignment matrix → annotated single-cell object with perturbation metadata

Hit calling from Perturb-seq screen — for each guide, test differential expression / perturbation effect vs non-targeting control, identify significant perturbation effects and rank guides by effect magnitude. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575. | perturbation effect testing per guide in a Perturb-seq CRISPR screen — differential expression of each guide vs non-targeting control, multiple-testing correction, effect size ranking → ranked list of significant perturbation effects per guide

Perturbation state embedding using scVI / scANVI — train variational inference model on perturbed single-cell transcriptomes accounting for batch effects and perturbation labels, produce latent space representation of perturbation states. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575. | scVI / scANVI latent embedding of perturbed single-cell transcriptomes — variational inference model trained on count matrix with batch covariates and perturbation labels, produce low-dimensional latent representation capturing perturbation states → embedded latent space for downstream comparison of perturbation effects
Find and rank drug targets for myasthenia gravis

Assign Perturb-seq sgRNA guides to single-cell barcodes | guide-to-cell barcode assignment and demultiplexing from Perturb-seq CRISPR guide capture data → cell-by-guide assignment table and filtered count matrix

Perform Perturb-seq hit calling and differential expression against non-targeting controls | statistical hit calling and differential expression scoring of perturbed cells versus non-targeting control guides → per-target effect sizes, p-values, and prioritized screen hits

Model perturbation states with scVI and scANVI latent space embedding | probabilistic latent space embedding and perturbation state representation learning using scVI and semi-supervised scANVI → low-dimensional perturbation space and state embeddings

Find tumor-reactive T cells in my scRNA-seq data (clustering, T cell annotation, TCR clonotype expansion, tumor-reactivity marker scoring) | single-cell RNA-seq analysis to identify tumor-reactive T cells — QC, clustering, T-cell subset annotation, TCR clonotype expansion analysis and tumor-reactivity marker scoring (CXCL13, ENTPD1/CD39, PDCD1, ITGAE/CD103) → annotated reactive T-cell clusters and expanded clonotypes

Predict neoantigens from tumor sequencing data (somatic variant calling, HLA typing, MHC-I binding prediction) | neoantigen prediction from tumor sequencing data — somatic variant calling (tumor vs matched normal), HLA typing, mutant peptide generation and MHC-I binding affinity prediction (netMHCpan/pVACseq) → ranked candidate neoantigen table

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to identify differentially expressed genes between conditions | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data (alignment, quantification, DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial model), two-group or multi-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change, adjusted p-values, and ranked gene list

ATAC-seq open chromatin accessibility analysis to identify accessible regulatory regions | ATAC-seq peak calling and accessibility quantification from paired-end FASTQ (alignment, Tn5 offset correction, MACS2 narrow peak calling, consensus peak set, accessibility scores) → peaks BED + accessibility matrix

ChIP-seq transcription factor binding analysis to identify TF binding peaks | ChIP-seq peak calling for transcription factor binding from paired-end FASTQ with input control (alignment, duplicate removal, MACS2 narrow peak calling, motif analysis) → TF binding peaks BED + signal tracks

Integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, linking regulatory peaks to target genes using fluentGenomics-style approach | integration of three omics layers — RNA-seq differential expression results (gene-level log2FC + padj), ATAC-seq accessibility peaks (BED + scores), and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks (BED) — peak-to-gene linking by genomic proximity or correlation, overlap of accessible regions with TF binding sites, identification of co-regulated gene regulatory modules → integrated regulatory map linking peaks to DEGs

Identify tumor-reactive T cells from scRNA-seq data | identification and phenotypic characterization of tumor-reactive or exhausted T cell states from single-cell RNA sequencing data → annotated T cell clusters, reactivity gene expression signatures, and clonal states

Predict candidate neoantigens from tumor sequencing data | tumor neoantigen identification and peptide-MHC binding affinity prediction from somatic variants and patient HLA types → prioritized candidate neoepitopes

Load EPIC/450K IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalisation | import and preprocess Illumina EPIC/450K methylation array IDAT files with minfi (read.metharray.exp → rgset), apply functional/noob normalisation → normalised Beta/M-value matrix and quality metrics

DSS-based differential methylation analysis on normalised methylation values | differential methylation analysis on a normalised methylation matrix (Beta/M-values from minfi or Bismark bisulfite coverage) using DSS — two-group comparison → differentially methylated loci (DML) and regions (DMR) with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

missMethyl gene-set enrichment on differential methylation results accounting for probe count bias | gene-set enrichment on differential methylation results using missMethyl (goseq-based bias correction for probe count and gene length) → enriched GO/KEGG gene sets with adjusted p-values

Guide assignment for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen — assign gRNAs to individual cells from single-cell CRISPR perturbation data (Replogle et al. 2022-style design) | guide RNA assignment to cells in a single-cell CRISPR perturbation screen (Perturb-seq) — quantify gRNA UMIs per cell, apply assignment thresholds, resolve multi-guide cells → cell-by-guide assignment matrix linked to the gene expression matrix

Hit calling on guide-assigned Perturb-seq data — identify perturbations with significant gene-expression effects versus non-targeting controls | perturbation hit calling on guide-assigned Perturb-seq data — per-perturbation differential expression testing against non-targeting control cells → ranked significant hits with effect sizes and FDR-adjusted p-values

Perturbation state analysis — scVI / scANVI latent embedding of Perturb-seq cells to define and annotate perturbation-induced cell states | latent embedding of single-cell perturbation states using scVI/scANVI variational autoencoders on hit-called Perturb-seq expression data with perturbation labels → integrated latent space, perturbation state clusters, label transfer and UMAP visualization

Graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference with Monocle3 (R) on the user's single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using the monocle_cluster and root_cell parameters | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on a processed single-cell AnnData object (Monocle3-style dimensionality reduction, clustering, principal graph learning from a user-specified root cell/cluster) → per-cell pseudotime values, trajectory plots (PNG), updated h5ad and pseudotime CSV

RNA velocity analysis with scVelo (Python) on the same single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using the velocity_mode parameter | RNA velocity estimation on a single-cell AnnData object with spliced/unspliced count layers (scVelo, mode selectable: dynamical / stochastic / steady-state) → per-cell velocity vectors, velocity stream and embedding plots (PNG), updated h5ad and velocity CSV

Load EPIC/450K methylation array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalisation | Illumina EPIC/450K methylation array preprocessing from raw IDAT files (minfi RGChannelSet loading, functional normalisation, probe filtering) → normalised beta/M-value methylation matrix

Run DSS differential methylation analysis on the normalised methylation matrix | differential methylation analysis on a normalised methylation matrix (DSS beta-binomial model), two-group comparison → differentially methylated loci and regions (DML/DMR) with statistics

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results | gene-set enrichment analysis (GO/KEGG) on differentially methylated CpGs/genes from methylation data, correcting for probe-number bias (missMethyl gometh) → enriched gene sets and pathways

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Identify tumor-reactive T cells from scRNA-seq data — T cell subset annotation, activation/exhaustion marker profiling, and TCR clonotype expansion analysis to distinguish tumor-reactive populations | Single-cell RNA-seq T cell subset identification and tumor-reactivity characterization — cell clustering, T cell marker annotation, activation/exhaustion signature scoring, TCR clonotype analysis if V(D)J data available → tumor-reactive T cell clusters with marker genes and clonotype expansion metrics

Predict neoantigens from tumor somatic mutation data — variant annotation, HLA binding affinity prediction, and expression filtering to rank candidate neoantigens | Neoantigen prediction pipeline from tumor somatic variants — peptide generation from missense/indel/fusion variants, HLA class I/II binding affinity prediction (NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan), expression and clonality filtering → ranked candidate neoantigen list with binding affinity and expression evidence

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal (rat, mouse, or dog) data using allometric scaling and interspecies extrapolation for PBPK model parameterization | Interspecies allometric scaling and PK parameter estimation from preclinical animal pharmacokinetic data (rat/mouse/dog CL, Vd, t_half) to predict human PK parameters — input: per-species PK parameters or concentration-time data → output: human PK parameter estimates (CL, Vd, Ka, etc.) for PBPK model

Run full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance, including optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing | Mechanistic physiologically-based pharmacokinetic simulation using a multi-compartmental model with organ-specific clearance (hepatic, renal) — input: human PK parameters from allometric scaling, compound properties (SMILES, fu, CLint, logP), optional organ impairment parameters → output: plasma concentration-time profiles, organ exposure, AUC/Cmax for general and special populations

Perform Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization of PBPK model predictions across population parameter distributions | Population variability characterization via Monte Carlo sampling over PBPK model parameter distributions (covariates, PK parameters, physiological parameters) — input: PBPK model from Step 2 with parameter uncertainty ranges → output: population distribution of PK metrics (AUC, Cmax, trough), percentile intervals, sensitivity analysis

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

PBPK Simulation — & Special Populations. Mechanistic PBPK simulation for predicting human pharmacokinetics from preclinical animal data. Step 1: to estimate human PK parameters from rat, mouse, or dog data. Step 2: full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance (optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing). Step 3: Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization. Use for: species scaling, IND/NDA PBPK packages, first-in-human dose projection, and special population (renal/hepatic impairment) dose adjustments. Required for regulator

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Run RNA-seq differential expression analysis to derive a transcriptional signature (up/down gene list) from user's samples | bulk RNA-seq differential expression pipeline — alignment, quantification, and DESeq2/edgeR two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values defining a transcriptional signature

Find drugs with transcriptional signatures matching the RNA-seq differential expression results (connectivity map / LINCS L1000 signature matching for drug repurposing) | drug repurposing via transcriptional signature matching — query a ranked gene signature (from DE results) against connectivity map / LINCS L1000 reference profiles → ranked list of compounds with similar or opposing expression signatures

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to generate a disease or condition transcriptional signature | differential gene expression analysis on RNA-seq data → ranked differentially expressed gene signature (up- and down-regulated genes)

Connectivity mapping to query the transcriptional signature against reference drug perturbation profiles | connectivity mapping and drug signature matching using an input differential expression signature against reference perturbation databases (CMAP / LINCS L1000) → prioritized candidate drugs

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to produce a transcriptional signature (treatment vs control DEGs with log2 fold changes) | bulk RNA-seq processing and differential gene expression (QC, alignment, quantification, DESeq2/edgeR two-group comparison) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values as a transcriptional signature

Find drugs whose transcriptional signatures match (or reverse) the RNA-seq signature from step 1 via connectivity mapping | signature-based drug repurposing / connectivity mapping — query a differential expression signature (up- and down-regulated gene sets) against drug perturbation signature databases (LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map) → ranked compounds with connectivity scores

Phase A — Compound physicochemical profiling and PK/exposure prediction for ICH S7A safety pharmacology simulation: molecular properties (MW, logP, logD, TPSA, HBD/HBA), predicted ADME (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion), and PK parameters (predicted human Cmax, AUC, plasma protein binding, volume of distribution, terminal half-life) to establish safety-margin baselines for downstream core battery assessments | physicochemical property profiling and systemic PK exposure prediction for a small-molecule compound — calculated properties, predicted human oral PK (Cmax, AUC, fu_plasma, Vd, t½) → exposure metrics for safety margin calculations across ICH S7A core battery endpoints

Phase A — Compound setup and in silico safety pharmacology profiling: take the test compound (SMILES), predict secondary pharmacology off-target panel hits and hERG liability, and derive dose levels for the in vivo core battery | in silico safety pharmacology profiling of a small molecule from SMILES — secondary pharmacology off-target panel prediction plus hERG cardiac liability scoring → off-target hit table and proposed low/mid/high dose levels for the in vivo core battery

Phase B — Cardiovascular core battery simulation: telemetry endpoints (arterial blood pressure, heart rate, ECG intervals PR/QRS/QT/QTc) at the Phase A dose levels | cardiovascular safety pharmacology core battery simulation per ICH S7A — in vivo telemetry endpoints (systolic/diastolic/mean arterial pressure, heart rate, ECG PR/QRS/QT/QTc intervals) across dose levels → dose-response cardiovascular endpoint tables with statistics vs vehicle

Phase C — Central nervous system core battery simulation: functional observational battery / modified Irwin test endpoints (locomotor activity, behavior, coordination, reflexes, body temperature) at the Phase A dose levels | central nervous system safety pharmacology core battery simulation per ICH S7A — functional observational battery / modified Irwin test endpoints (spontaneous locomotor activity, behavioral changes, motor coordination, sensory-motor reflexes, body temperature) across dose levels → CNS endpoint score tables with statistics vs vehicle

Phase D — Respiratory core battery simulation plus integrated assessment: plethysmography endpoints (respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute ventilation) and a combined cross-system statistical analysis with a GLP-style safety pharmacology summary report | respiratory safety pharmacology core battery simulation per ICH S7A — whole-body plethysmography endpoints (respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute ventilation) across dose levels, followed by integrated cross-system (cardiovascular + CNS + respiratory) statistical analysis → respiratory endpoint tables and a combined GLP-style core battery safety pharmacology report

Validate a SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) for the MMP pipeline | SMILES input validation and parsing — read a text file of SMILES strings with compound IDs, canonicalise each molecule via RDKit, reject invalid entries, emit a validated SMILES+ID table

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffold + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic decomposition via RDKit — break validated molecules at retrosynthetic bonds into core scaffolds and attached R-group fragments, output scaffold–R-group fragment pairs

mmpdb property-delta calculation for fragment swaps from RECAP decomposition output | Matched Molecular Pair analysis with mmpdb — build MMP database from scaffold–fragment pairs, compute property deltas for fragment transformations, output per-transformation delta predictions

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and SA score from mmpdb output | Scaffold ranking — count scaffold frequencies across the fragment set, compute drug-likeness (e.g. QED/Lipinski) and synthetic accessibility (SA) scores per scaffold, output a ranked scaffold table sorted by composite score

Phase A: Pharmacokinetic and exposure modeling to determine clinical unbound Cmax and tissue distribution | physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) exposure simulation from molecular SMILES and in vitro ADME parameters → predicted unbound plasma Cmax and target tissue concentration profiles

Phase B: Cardiovascular system safety assessment covering cardiac ion channel inhibition and QTc liability | in silico cardiac ion channel inhibition panel screening (hERG/IKr, Nav1.5, Cav1.2) coupled to ventricular action potential electrophysiology simulation → QTc prolongation risk and arrhythmia safety margins

Phase C: Central nervous system (CNS) safety profiling for neurobehavioral liabilities and off-target neurotoxicity | in silico blood-brain barrier permeability prediction and neuroreceptor off-target binding profiling (GABA, NMDA, dopaminergic, serotonergic panels) → CNS exposure, seizure liability, and Irwin/FOB neurofunctional risk scores

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata for downstream limma-voom DE and GSVA/ssGSEA analysis | input validation and QC of a gene expression matrix and associated clinical metadata — check matrix format, sample-metadata alignment, missing values, low-count filtering, and normalisation status → cleaned expression matrix and metadata ready for limma-voom

Voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes moderation, and topTable extraction of logFC and adj.P.Val | differential expression analysis on a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix using limma-voom — voom transformation, linear model fitting with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation (eBayes), topTable extraction → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

GSVA/ssGSEA gene set enrichment on MSigDB hallmark gene sets (50 gene sets), identifying top enriched pathways per group | gene set variation analysis on a gene expression matrix using GSVA/ssGSEA method against MSigDB hallmark collection (50 gene sets) — compute per-sample enrichment scores, rank top enriched pathways per group → pathway-level enrichment matrix and ranked pathway lists

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) for the Matched Molecular Pair pipeline | validation and standardization of a line-delimited SMILES+ID input file (parse with RDKit, flag invalid/duplicate structures, sanitize) → clean validated compound table

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated compounds into scaffolds + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic fragmentation of validated small molecules with RDKit → scaffold cores and R-group fragments per compound

mmpdb matched molecular pair analysis: compute property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair transform extraction and property-delta statistics with mmpdb on fragmented compounds → MMP transform database with per-swap property changes

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA score) | scaffold prioritization from MMP results — rank novel scaffolds by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness (QED-style descriptors), and synthetic accessibility score → ranked scaffold hit list

Validate the gene expression matrix and matched clinical metadata (sample matching, missing values, distribution checks) | validation and QC of a gene expression matrix with matched clinical/sample metadata — dimension checks, sample-ID matching, missing-value and distribution assessment → validated analysis-ready expression matrix and metadata table

Run limma-voom differential expression: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, topTable (logFC, adj.P.Val) | differential gene expression on a bulk expression matrix using limma-voom (voom precision-weight transformation, linear model with covariate adjustment, empirical Bayes moderation) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values via topTable

Run GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring on MSigDB hallmark gene sets (50 sets); report top enriched pathways per group | gene set variation analysis (GSVA/ssGSEA) scoring of the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets on a normalized expression matrix → per-sample pathway enrichment scores and top enriched pathways per group
Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) | validation and sanitization of input chemical SMILES identifiers and structure records → cleaned SMILES and metadata
RDKit RECAP decomposition into scaffold + R-groups | fragmentation of chemical compounds into core scaffolds and R-group substituents using RDKit RECAP rules → fragment tables and scaffold mappings
mmpdb: property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair analysis calculating property deltas across fragment transformation rules using mmpdb → MMP index and property delta tables

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, SA score | scoring and ranking of novel chemical scaffolds based on frequency, QED drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score → prioritized scaffold table

Validate RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata alignment | data validation and quality control of expression count matrix and clinical metadata table (sample matching, missing value checks, format verification)

Perform limma-voom differential expression analysis including covariates | differential gene expression testing using limma-voom (voom transformation, linear modeling with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation, topTable extraction) → log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

Perform GSVA or ssGSEA signature scoring on MSigDB Hallmark gene sets | single-sample pathway enrichment scoring using GSVA/ssGSEA on normalized expression data against MSigDB Hallmark 50 gene sets → pathway enrichment score matrix and top enriched pathways per group
